definition: Block-level replication copies changed portions of disk data from a source server to a destination.
A staging area subnet contains the replication resources that maintain source-server data in AWS.
RPO expresses how recent the recoverable replicated data is relative to the source.
RTO expresses the time required to recover service after a disruption.
A crash-consistent recovery point contains disk data as if the server had stopped without flushing memory.
A point-in-time snapshot preserves replicated disk data from a particular moment for recovery.
Failover redirects traffic from a primary system to a recovery system.
Failback redirects traffic from recovery systems to restored primary systems.
Reverse replication copies recovery-system changes back to the primary systems before failback.
A launch template supplies EC2 settings such as the subnet for drill and recovery instances.
An ISO is a bootable image used to start the Failback Client on a destination server.
